value.name: Daniel distinguishes Rosa's testimony
value.description: Daniel insists that Rosa merely says she saw the room, framing her account as testimony rather than direct proof.

value.name: Asha judges Daniel's wording
value.description: Asha internally recognizes Daniel's phrasing as a way of reducing Rosa to a category rather than treating her as an equal witness.
evidence: there was something in the way Daniel had pitched the word — *says* — that had nothing to do with disagreement and everything to do with reducing her to a category.

value.name: Lucia rebukes Daniel
value.description: Lucia finally speaks up and tells Daniel not to treat Rosa that way, especially not in front of others.
evidence: Lucia spoke for the first time since they had come down the stairs.
"Don't do that. Don't do that to her. Not in front of —"

value.name: Lucia rejects conditional respect
value.description: Lucia stops herself from saying 'strangers' and insists Daniel should not do this at all, regardless of who is present.
evidence: She did not say *not in front of strangers,* because Asha was a stranger and Marcus was a stranger and Lucia perhaps did not want to imply that the not-doing was conditional on strangers being absent.

value.name: Daniel defends his statement as legal truth
value.description: Daniel denies wrongdoing and argues that he is only stating the legally correct distinction between a witness and a document.
evidence: "I'm not doing anything. I'm saying what is legally true. Rosa is a witness. A witness's testimony is not the same as a document."

value.name: Daniel seeks legal confirmation
value.description: Daniel appeals to the counselor to confirm his legal distinction and receives agreement.
evidence: "Counselor — you'll back me up on this — a witness who saw a document being prepared is not the same as a document. Yes?"
"That is correct as far as it goes."

value.name: Daniel claims he only meant the legal point
value.description: After the counselor agrees, Daniel asserts that this legal distinction is all he was saying.
evidence: "There. That is all I am saying."

value.name: Lucia challenges Daniel's tone
value.description: Lucia tells Daniel that his wording carried a different, more insulting meaning than the legal point he claims.
evidence: "You said it differently than that," Lucia said quietly.

value.name: Lucia accuses Daniel of patronizing Rosa
value.description: Lucia explains that Daniel's phrasing echoed how he used to dismiss their mother, implying he was treating Rosa as someone to be brushed aside.
evidence: "You said *Rosa says.* You said it the way you used to say *Mami says* when we were children and you didn't want to do something she had asked you to do."

value.name: Lucia begins a sharper accusation
value.description: Lucia starts to say that Daniel spoke as if Rosa were something lesser, escalating the confrontation.
